newsitem.title: INDIA: India monsoon seen normal, late in oilseed regions.
newsitem.headline: India monsoon seen normal, late in oilseed regions.

text.p: The progress of southwest monsoon rains is satisfactory over most of India but the rains are inadequate for sowing operations to start in some oilseeds areas, weather and trade officials said on Tuesday.
"At this stage, progress of monsoon rains has been quite satisfactory," Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) director S.C. Goel told Reuters.

Goel said monsoon rains had covered most of the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, and most regions in the central state of Madhya Pradesh and the western state of Gujarat.
"Rains have been excellent in the Saurashtra region," said Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd. "Sowing operations (for the groundnut crop) have already started."
Saurashtra is the main groundnut-growing region in Gujarat, which contributes about 35 percent of India's groundnut output.
Although weather officials said rains had covered most parts of the four southern states, industry officials said the monsoon was still deficient in some regions in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.

"(Groundnut) sowing has been delayed in these two states as rains are still less than needed to start sowing," Shah said. Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh account for 35 percent to the country's groundnut production.
Industry officials said rainfall was so far adequate in the rice-growing regions of the northern states of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Punjab.
"Sowing in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh has already started," said Prem Garg, managing director of Shivnath Harnarayan, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter. "In other parts, it will start by next week."
Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh are India's major rice producers. They also contribute about 10 percent of the country's oilseed output.
Weather officials said monsoon rains had covered the entire country except for some parts of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh in the north.
"The progress of monsoon rains this week will also be normal," Goel said. "I expect more areas of Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan to be covered this week."
IMD officials said they were not worried about the impact of El Nino warm water currents on the progress of monsoon rains.
"We are not much worried about El Nino at this stage," Goel said without elaborating.
El Nino raises the water temperature off the coast of South America and can disrupt weather patterns worldwide.

The IMD last month forecast a 10th successive normal monsoon in 1997 but it also said El Nino, which is one of the 16 parameters on which its monsoon forecast is based, was showing an "unfavourable trend" this year.
